LESSON: WRITING 9.4.1 PUNCTUATION: THE HYPHEN

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.4: Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation: The Hyphen
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation: The Hyphen, part of Strand 9 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why do we punctuate texts? 2) How do we use hyphens in sentences?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify grade appropriate hyphenated words from a written text,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation: The Hyphen in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use grade appropriate hyphenated words correctly for clarity of meaning,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation: The Hyphen in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. judge sentences for correctness of language, and use of the hyphen. ● Learner is guided to identify hyphenated words from a text. ● In groups, learners are to search for hyphenated words such as dark-blue shirt, good-looking, good- hearted, fast-moving, anti- clockwise from the internet using digital devices with assistive technology, braille/appropriate print magazines, newspapers, textbooks or brochures. ● Learner is guided to listen to a dictation of the following words: mother- in-law, father-- in law, sister-in -law, brother -in - law and write them down. ● In pairs, learners are guided to listen to an audio recording of the words mother-in-law, father- in law, sister-in - law, brother -in – law and anti-clockwise and create a list. ● Learner is guided to use words such as fast- flowing, slow-moving, open-mouthed, big eyed, sugar-free among others in sentences. 1) Why do we punctuate texts? 2) How do we use hyphens in sentences? 58 ● Learners are guided to hyphenate words which refer to age such as five- year-old girl, two-year-old, middle-aged man. ● Learners are guided to use the hyphen correctly when writing numbers 21 through 99: for example. Twenty-one; ninety-nine ● Learner is guided to create a poster displaying the words, mother in law, father-- in law, sister-in - law, brother -in –law, anti- clockwise among others. ● Learners are guided in groups to make charts and posters featuring hyphenated words and phrases such as fast- flowing river, slow- moving train, good-looking among others. ● Note: The learner should only be exposed to simple and common hyphenated words. Again, the focus should be on the usage of the words in sentences.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 9.4.1 Punctuation: The Hyphen in the Kenya CBC curriculum.

4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.
